Trump spoke after meeting with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, a key intermediary with Tehran, as efforts to end the war ramp up following last week's US midterm election. More than eight months into the conflict he launched alongside Israel on Feb 28, Trump has played down the likelihood of major warfare restarting soon but remains unwilling to accept an existing Iranian truce plan. Senior US and Gulf officials have cast doubt on the chances of an imminent deal. Mutual attacks continue, with the US striking Iran's Qeshm island overnight, according to Iranian state media, and Iran attacking tankers in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz this month while its Yemeni Houthi allies have hit Saudi Arabia.

DIPLOMATIC MOVES Al-Thani, who is both prime minister and foreign minister of Qatar, met Trump after visiting Tehran last week. The prime minister called his talks with both Trump and Vice President JD Vance positive. "Grateful for the positive discussions on reaching a deal and bringing peace to the region," he said on X. Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei said on X the US should "stop manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks" and that it was "time to surrender to the seven conditions Iran has repeatedly set out". Iran's proposal to end the war involves an end to the US blockade of its ports, the lifting of some sanctions and a halt to bombing in return for Tehran stopping its own blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, with talks on its nuclear programme and other sanctions to follow. The US has repeatedly rejected that plan, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio describing Tehran's conditions on Sunday as "outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic". Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei defended the plan on Monday as the most reasonable offer on the table. Senior US Republicans including Vice President JD Vance have blamed their party's losses in last week's elections on the Iran war. Despite the growing domestic political pressure to end the conflict, Rubio said he did not believe a diplomatic breakthrough was imminent. A senior United Arab Emirates official, Anwar Gargash, echoed that view on Monday, saying a comprehensive political settlement between the US and Iran appeared difficult. "We should ... prepare for a long period of uncertainty in which neither a decisive resolution nor stable regional order can be taken for granted," he said. Vance, who led the negotiations for a short-lived truce in June, will also meet Al-Thani, whose country has been a prime mediator since early in the war, conveying messages between the sides and proposing ways to bridge their differences.

Anxiety over the war has pervaded the region for months, and Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said on Monday he had told Trump that Ankara did not want to see a new escalation. "We emphasise at every opportunity that it is possible to resolve these issues through dialogue and diplomacy. Unfortunately, we see a negative shift once again. We are doing our utmost to prevent this," Erdogan told reporters. MILITARY ACTION Sunday night's strikes on Qeshm island did not impact vital infrastructure or services, a provincial official told Iran's semi-official Fars news agency on Monday. The US has not commented on the Iranian media reports. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that US strikes were targeting Iranian radar systems serving both air defence and ship navigation, as well as bases for missile launchers and mine-laying systems. Attacks on tankers in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz ramped up sharply in October and have continued at the highest rate since the start of the war, figures from international maritime agencies showed last week. Iran, which typically does not acknowledge striking vessels that report being hit by projectiles, said on Sunday a tanker had hit a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz. A state television reporter said on Monday that 11 tankers had been "disabled" over the past 10 days.

１株当たり１．７８ドルと、ＬＳＥＧがまとめたアナリスト予想平均１．５９ドルを上回った。業界では金利上昇を受けて資産売却が鈍化する中、資産売却を積極的に進めたことが寄与した。資金運用による手数料関連利益は２７％増の１３億ドルだった。

２６年の投資家への還元額は４００億ドルを超える見通しで、これまでの年間最高を大幅に上回る水準となる。発表を受けて、株価は時間外取引で一時３％上昇した。

ＫＫＲの共同最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）、ジョセフ・ベイ氏とスコット・ナトール氏は「引き続き投資を収益化していく」と表明した。

２６年７─９月期は、データセンターや民間航空インフラに関連する企業の売却など、取引の完了が相次いだ。米ＵＳＩインシュアランス・サービシズを保険仲介大手のエーオンに約１７０億ドルで売却する取引は２６年９─１２月期中に完了見通しで、取引による調整後利益は２０億ドル程度の見込み。

２６年７─９月期に新規資金として２５０億ドルを調達し、２６年９月末の運用資産総額は８０００億ドルを超えている。

ＫＫＲは３０年までに資産運用残高を１兆ドル台に乗せることを目指している。

Nov 9 : On the streets of Taipei and Seoul, fans of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang mob him for autographs on books, posters and sometimes even on their bodies. In private, even billionaires Larry Ellison and Elon Musk were once reduced to "begging" for his coveted AI chips. The star power that 63-year-old Huang draws as the gatekeeper to Nvidia's chips shows how badly the AI industry is leaning on him for the graphics processing units that train models and run services such as ChatGPT. But he is not just a chip supplier; instead Nvidia has in recent years turned its swelling cash pile into a war chest to fund companies ranging from AI cloud-computing providers and suppliers to the biggest labs. Analysts say that makes Huang a potential risk to the AI industry as Nvidia investigates whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence after Huang confirmed his affair with a Chinese businesswoman accused of passing information to Beijing.

"It is hard not to read the news over the weekend as negative given it brings the stewardship of one of America's most important companies and the architect of the US AI trajectory under debate," Stacy Rasgon, analyst at Bernstein, said. "Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he is Nvidia, clearly sets the long-term strategy and direction, and pulls most of the company's strings himself." VOCAL AI CHAMPION Such is Huang's spell that a casual night of fried chicken and beer in Seoul with the CEOs of Samsung and Hyundai last year sent the shares of two South Korean food companies soaring, while his endorsement of Marvell Technology as the next "trillion-dollar company" propelled the shares of the custom chipmaker to record highs. As a leading counterweight to AI skeptics, Huang has often dismissed fears of a bubble and challenged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's apocalyptic warning that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity. Any setback for Huang could deprive the AI industry of one of its most vocal champions who has often argued that the technology would transform everything from computing and manufacturing to healthcare and robotics. AI'S CHIP ALLOCATOR-IN-CHIEF AND A POWERFUL BOSS Huang's influence goes beyond talking up AI. He holds sway over the supply of the chips that can determine how fast AI companies spending tens of billions of dollars can grow. That status was validated by Oracle co-founder Ellison in September 2024 when he recounted a dinner at Nobu in Palo Alto. "I would describe the dinner as me and Elon begging Jensen for GPUs," Ellison told analysts. "Please take our money ... We need you to take more of our money." Huang has a firm grip on Nvidia, which he runs through an unusually flat structure, with dozens of executives reporting directly to him. However, as its fifth-largest shareholder with a roughly 3.6 per cent stake, he does not have special voting shares that give founders such as Meta Platforms' Mark Zuckerberg and SpaceX's Elon Musk majority control of their companies. "A lot of companies' organization charts, they all look the same. And it doesn't make any sense to me. The architecture of the company should reflect the environment in which it exists," Huang said on the Lex Fridman Podcast in March. He said more than 60 executives report to him, nearly all in engineering roles, including experts in memory chips, networking and graphics and central processors. Huang's family is also woven into Nvidia, with son-in-law Nico Caprez overseeing ties with neoclouds and data-center operators as vice president of global AI infrastructure growth. Huang's daughter Madison is a senior director overseeing marketing for Nvidia's physical AI products and often accompanies him on business trips, while his son Spencer works in the robotics division. NO IMMEDIATE SUCCESSOR Analysts have said Huang, who has run Nvidia since co-founding the chip designer in 1993, has no clear successor. The company, which said over the weekend Huang has the board's backing, has not disclosed a succession plan. "Jensen is not replaceable... there is no other person on the management team bench that can step in seamlessly as CEO," said long-time technology bull Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co. Besides Huang, Nvidia lists four executives on its leadership page. The best known is finance chief Colette Kress, who often represents the company at investor conferences. The others are executive vice president of worldwide field operations Nick Parker, executive vice president of operations Debora Shoquist and Tim Teter, executive vice president, general counsel and secretary.

The paper, founded by the last Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev with money from his 1990 Nobel Peace Prize, had kept going until now despite a sharp tightening of censorship after Russia launched its full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022. DUBAI: Iran defended a proposal on Monday (Nov 9) to restart peace talks in as few as two days as the most reasonable offer on the table, after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called some of Iran's conditions "outrageous and ridiculous". "Is it unreasonable that Iran demands that US illegal sanctions and its naval blockade must be lifted before negotiations start and that the war should end on all fronts?" Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a weekly press conference in response to Rubio's remarks. Iran has made the offer to shorten the time to restart talks from an earlier seven-day proposal, which calls for Washington to first meet conditions including halting hostilities, lifting a blockade and waiving sanctions. Baghaei also said US pressure on Iraq to close most of its borders with Iran should not affect bilateral ties with Baghdad, after Iraq's foreign minister said Washington was pushing for such a move. Baghaei dismissed a US military task force aimed at restricting Iran's land trade as a diversion following President Donald Trump 's Republicans' losses in midterm elections.

PARIS: A G7 foreign ministers gathering in Paris on Monday (Nov 9) will provide the first opportunity for Washington's allies to gauge whether a US midterm defeat for President Donald Trump alters the administration's approach to Ukraine, the Middle East and ties with its closest partners, four G7 diplomats said. The diplomats signalled the Democrats' gains could narrow the White House's room for manoeuvre but warned against expecting a return to traditional US multilateralism while foreign policy remains very much under Trump's control. The meeting, moved at short notice from Marseille to Paris for security reasons after weeks of protests across France , will see US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, viewed as a potential 2028 presidential contender, make his first appearance before allies since the elections. Other than France, the G7 includes Britain, Canada, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, as well as the European Union. Ministers from Ukraine, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Korea and Brazil are also attending.

With Ukraine top of the agenda, the G7 ministerial comes ahead of trilateral discussions on Tuesday in Abu Dhabi between Ukraine, Russia and the United States.  Officials from France, Britain, Germany, NATO and the European Commission are also aiming to be in the Emirati capital, although they are not expected to take part in the trilateral format.

In a sign of friction among Europeans, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni warned on Nov 5 that Europe risks becoming irrelevant in efforts to end the war in Ukraine if member states continue pursuing separate diplomatic tracks rather than agreeing on a common representative and strategy, an issue that is likely to come up at the G7. Diplomats painted a sombre picture of the situation in Ukraine. While the front had largely stabilised, making major breakthroughs unlikely, they warned that Russia had shifted tactics toward systematically targeting energy infrastructure in an effort to trigger a nationwide winter blackout. Shortages of Patriot interceptors and other air-defence systems were Kyiv's most urgent military vulnerability and they said one objective of the G7 meeting would be to sustain pressure on Russia while mobilising additional military, financial and energy support for Ukraine. Iran is also expected to feature prominently in discussions. Washington's G7 allies have repeatedly voiced scepticism over the war and fear further US military action could worsen rather than resolve the crisis. The talks could also expose differences between Paris and Washington over Lebanon. France is pushing for discussions on a new UN-backed security framework to replace current arrangements in southern Lebanon and has floated options including a French-Italian international force. While French officials privately acknowledge US reluctance to embrace some of those ideas, diplomats said the G7 offers an opportunity for the allies to narrow differences as the expiry of existing arrangements at the end of the year draws nearer.
